To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the thermal motion of a single atom is a Gaussian distribution of displacements from its equilibrium position in a crystal structure, (ii) its shape is an ellipsoid, (iii) the shape of this ellipsoid is defined by the three principal axes of the thermal motion, (iv) these principal axes can be determined experimentally by X-ray diffraction analysis, (v) the lengths of the principal axes of an ellipsoid of thermal motion can be used to determine the potential energy function
the thermal motions of atoms and ions in crystal structures can be represented in terms of three orthogonal displacement vectors, each of which can be represented as an ellipsoid of revolution.
the thermal ellipsoids of the three atoms in the title compound are elongated along the a axis, and are not equivalent.

understanding the nature of the forces which act between atoms in molecules and in crystals.
understanding the physical basis for the thermal motion of atoms in crystals.
the development and application of methods for the analysis of crystallographic data, particularly those arising from single-crystal and powder diffraction experiments.

the analysis of thermal motion of atoms in crystals is a valuable tool for understanding the structure of matter, and can yield important physical information.

the thermal motion of atoms in crystals, which is a consequence of the random thermal motions of the atoms, can be analysed to yield physical information, such as atomic mean-square displacement, mean-square atomic volume change, and the anisotropy and asymmetry of atomic thermal motions.
